transcript.content: Hello, I'm glad you could make it in today. What brings you to see me?

Hi, doctor. Thanks. Well, I'm here because I'm having some trouble with my eating. What really worries me is that once I start picking at food late at night, I just can't seem to stop. I'll tell myself, 'That's enough, Santiago,' but my hand just keeps going back for more. It's like... like I don't get to make the decision anymore. So, I figured I should come in and talk to someone about it.
After these episodes of eating, do you do anything to try to compensate or prevent weight gain, such as making yourself throw up or taking laxatives?
No, I don't do anything like that. I've never made myself throw up or taken laxatives or pills or anything. I usually just... well, I just eat all that food and then eventually go to bed.
Do you feel like you need to eat in order to fall asleep?

No, I wouldn't say that. I don't eat specifically to help me sleep. It's more just... I happen to be up, and I start picking at things, and then it gets out of hand. But I don't feel like I actually need the food to nod off. It just ends up being the last thing I do before I finally go to bed.
Do you usually have an appetite or eat breakfast in the morning?
No, I don't really have much of an appetite when I wake up. I usually just skip breakfast altogether. I mean, after eating so much the night before, I just don't feel hungry in the morning.
How long has this pattern of late-night eating been going on?

It's been about 10 months now. It started right around the time my aunt moved into the apartment. Ever since she got there, there just always seems to be extra food around the place, and... yeah, that's when this whole pattern really began.
